title: Count the Number of Ways to Make an Amount
real_world_story: A payment system wants to analyze how many different combinations of supported coin denominations can be used to make a particular payment amount.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Available coin denominations and the target payment amount
real_world_connection.target_represents: The number of distinct combinations that can produce the target amount
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Building the number of valid combinations for every amount using previously calculated results

problem_statement: Given N coin denominations and a target amount, find the number of distinct combinations that can be used to make the target amount. Each denomination can be used any number of times, and different orders of the same coins are considered the same combination.
task: Calculate the total number of distinct coin combinations that can produce the target amount.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of coin denominations. The second line contains N space-separated positive integers representing the denominations. The third line contains the target amount.
output_format: Print the number of distinct combinations that can form the target amount. If no combination exists, print 0.
constraints: Each coin denomination can be used multiple times

expected_algorithm.name: Dynamic Programming
expected_algorithm.reason: The number of ways to form each smaller amount can be reused to calculate the number of combinations for the target amount.

hint: Create a DP array where dp[x] stores the number of ways to form amount x.
Initialize dp[0] as 1 because there is one way to make amount zero.
Process each denomination and update the combinations for increasing amounts.
The final value at dp[target] is the required number of combinations.
real_world_takeaway: Dynamic Programming allows payment systems to analyze many possible currency combinations efficiently without recalculating the same smaller amounts repeatedly.
